name: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health
agency: CDC National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion, Division of Population Health
description: Model-based small-area estimates (multilevel regression and poststratification of BRFSS with ACS poverty and Census population) for 40 adult measures: 12 health outcomes, 7 prevention, 4 risk behaviors, 7 disability, 3 health status, 7 health-related social needs; crude and age-adjusted prevalence with 95% CIs. 2025 release Socrata IDs: county swc5-untb; place eav7-hnsx; tract cwsq-ngmh; ZCTA qnzd-25i4 (GIS-friendly wide format: i46a-9kgh; vgc8-iyc4; yjkw-uj5s; kee5-23sr). Archived 2024 release: fu4u-a9bh; sd8v-uq83; ai6z-tcin; 4r2x-hcfq. Archived 2023 release: h3ej-a9ec; krqc-563j; em5e-5hvn; 9umn-c3jf. Long-format fields (county): year; stateabbr; statedesc; locationname; datasource; category; measure; data_value_unit; data_value_type; data_value; data_value_footnote_symbol; data_value_footnote; low_confidence_limit; high_confidence_limit; totalpopulation; totalpop18plus; locationid; categoryid; measureid; datavaluetypeid; short_question_text; geolocation (tract adds countyname and countyfips; ZCTA omits state fields)
access_requirements: None (Socrata SODA API, no key; page with $limit and $offset; 2025 tract table has 3,047,284 rows)
license: Public Domain (data.cdc.gov dataset metadata)
time_coverage: PLACES releases 2020-2025 covering BRFSS data years 2017-2023 (2025 release: BRFSS 2023 for 35 measures and 2022 for 5); predecessor 500 Cities releases 2016-2019 (500 largest cities and their tracts)
update_cadence: Annual release (2025 release rows loaded 2025-12-04); current dataset IDs are overwritten each year and prior releases are re-published under new IDs
history_notes: 2024 release moved to 2020 Census geography (tracts, ZCTAs, places) and Connecticut planning regions (2023 release had 72,337 tracts, 2025 release 83,522); 2023 release added 7 disability measures and changed the CI simulation (wider CIs); 2024 release added 7 social-needs measures and dropped KIDNEY, CERVICAL, COREM, COREW; ISOLATION renamed LONELINESS in 2025; DEPRESSION and GHLTH first appear in 2021 release
suppression_rules: Values suppressed where population is under 50 (footnote *); 2023-BRFSS measures missing for Kentucky and Pennsylvania in the 2025 release; social-needs measures only for the 39 states + DC that fielded the BRFSS social determinants module
limitations: Model-based estimates, not direct survey values; CDC cautions against using them for program or policy evaluation and states the approach cannot track local change over time; release-to-release differences mix real change with method, input-year and geography changes; BRFSS 2024 excluded TN and BRFSS 2025 excluded CA, MS and NV, which may leave gaps in later releases
doc_evidence: Methodology page: MRP model, 1,000 Monte Carlo draws, 95% CI; Socrata metadata: 'This dataset contains model-based county estimates' using BRFSS 2023/2022
sample_evidence: $limit=3 rows from each of 4 IDs; county table 229,298 rows, 3,145 counties; Drew Co AR arthritis 2023 crude 29.9% (CI 26.6-33.3)

name: BRFSS Prevalence Data (2011 to present)
agency: CDC National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion, Division of Population Health
description: Direct weighted survey estimates from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System: crude prevalence with 95% CI and sample size for each question and response by state, territory and nationwide, with age, sex, race/ethnicity, education and income breakouts (Socrata dttw-5yxu; age-adjusted variant d2rk-yvas; metro/micro area SMART data j32a-sa6u)
license: Public Domain (data.cdc.gov dataset metadata)
time_coverage: 2011-2025 annual (2025 data released August 2026)
history_notes: 2011 introduced raking weights and the cell-phone sample; CDC states later data are not directly comparable with years before 2011; some questions are asked only in alternate years or in optional state modules
suppression_rules: Footnote fields present (data_value_footnote_symbol, data_value_footnote); suppression thresholds not verified
limitations: State level only (small-area values come from PLACES models); self-reported; jurisdictions dropped for not meeting minimum requirements: KY and PA (2023), TN (2024), CA, MS, NV and VI (2025)
doc_evidence: 2025 BRFSS page: released Aug 2026; CA, MS, NV, VI did not meet minimum requirements; not directly comparable to years before 2011
sample_evidence: dttw-5yxu: 3,211,643 rows, years 2011-2025; 2025 DIABETE4 overall rows lack CA, MS, NV; AL 2024 alcohol (ages 18-24) 49.07% CI 42.13-56.01

name: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI)
agency: CDC/ATSDR Geospatial Research, Analysis, and Services Program (GRASP)
description: Percentile rankings (0-1) of social vulnerability for census tracts and counties (and ZCTAs in 2022) built from 16 ACS 5-year variables in 4 themes (socioeconomic status; household characteristics; racial and ethnic minority status; housing type and transportation), with E_ estimates, EP_ percentages, M_ and MP_ margins of error, theme ranks RPL_THEME1-4, overall rank RPL_THEMES and F_ flags (90th percentile or higher); US files rank nationally and state files rank within state
license: No explicit license found; U.S. federal government work; CDC requests a suggested citation
update_cadence: Every 2 years since 2014 (2022 is latest; files last modified 2024-11-25)
history_notes: Ranks are relative within each release, so CDC says percentile scores are not comparable across years; 2000 built from Census 2000, 2010 onward from ACS 5-year; 2020 redesign added below-150%-poverty, housing cost burden and no-health-insurance variables, dropped per capita income, and moved limited English to theme 2; tract boundaries differ for 2000, 2010-2018 and 2020-2022
limitations: Relative index rather than an absolute measure; ACS inputs have large MOEs in small tracts; national and state-ranked files give different values; published corrections (2022 MP_CROWD; 2020 housing burden and overall SVI)
doc_evidence: Download page lists 2000-2022 and says 'percentile scores of different tracts in different years are not comparable'; 2022 documentation: 2018-2022 ACS, -999 missing
sample_evidence: Range request (6 KB) of SVI_2022_US_county.csv (2.3 MB): 158 columns; Autauga County AL RPL_THEMES 0.2663, EP_UNINSUR 7.4; ZCTA and 2000-2018 files return HTTP 200

name: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE)
agency: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Estimates Branch
description: Model-based single-year estimates of health insurance coverage (numbers and percents insured and uninsured, with 90% MOEs and CI bounds) for the nation, states and all counties, for ages under 65 by age group (AGECAT), sex (SEXCAT), income-to-poverty category (IPRCAT) and, for states only, race/ethnicity (RACECAT); combines ACS with federal tax returns, SNAP and Medicaid/CHIP records, County Business Patterns and census data; county estimates are adjusted to sum to state totals
access_requirements: Census API key (developer page: all Census Data API queries now require a key); keyless bulk CSV zips at https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/sahie/datasets/time-series/estimates-acs/
license: CC0 1.0 public domain dedication (Census API catalog license field)
time_coverage: 2008-2024 consistent ACS-based series (2024 estimates released August 2026); API temporal range 2006-2024 also includes pre-ACS 2006-2007 estimates
history_notes: Methodology switched to ACS-based inputs starting with 2008 estimates and Census advises against comparing them with earlier years; 2013 method-comparison file published; revised 2023 supplemental file (sahie-2023-sup) posted with the 2024 release in August 2026
limitations: Under-65 population only; race/ethnicity detail only for states; model-based with wide intervals for small counties; coverage reflects ACS status at time of interview
doc_evidence: SAHIE About page: consistent estimates 2008 to 2024 from ACS, tax returns, SNAP, Medicaid/CHIP; API variables.json lists PCTUI_PT, NUI_PT, AGECAT, IPRCAT
sample_evidence: Census API requires a key; verified by project adapter

name: American Community Survey 5-year estimates (disability, health insurance, SNAP receipt tables)
agency: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Direct survey estimates with 90% MOEs from ACS detailed tables. Verified in the 2024 5-year table shells: disability B18101 (sex by age by disability status), B18102-B18107 (hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, independent living), C18108 (number of disabilities), B18135 (disability by health insurance), C18130 (disability by poverty), C18120 (employment by disability); health insurance B27001, B27010 (types of coverage by age), C27007 (Medicaid/means-tested coverage), C27012 (coverage by work experience), C27016 (coverage by income-to-poverty ratio); SNAP B22001, B22003, B22010
access_requirements: Census API key; keyless bulk alternative is the table-based summary file at https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/
license: CC0 1.0 public domain dedication (Census API catalog license field)
time_coverage: 5-year periods through 2020-2024 (released January 2026); SNAP question asked since the 2005 ACS; current disability questions and health insurance question since the 2008 ACS, so the first comparable 5-year period is 2008-2012

suppression_rules: Block-group rows absent for B18101, C18108, C27007, B27001 and B22001 but present for B27010 (checked in 2024 summary file)

name: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death (NVSS mortality)
agency: CDC National Center for Health Statistics (via CDC WONDER)
description: Final death counts, crude and age-adjusted death rates (2000 U.S. standard population by default) and 95% CIs from U.S. resident death certificates, by underlying cause (ICD-10, e.g., 113 selected causes), age, sex, race and Hispanic origin, year and place of residence; single-race database 2018-2024 and bridged-race database 1999-2020
access_requirements: Interactive query form; user must accept the NCHS data-use restrictions; the WONDER API returns only national vital statistics (no state, county or urbanization grouping)
license: NCHS data-use restrictions: no attempt to identify persons; do not present or publish statistics representing nine or fewer deaths
time_coverage: 1999-2024 final data (single race 2018-2024; bridged race 1999-2020); 2024 final deaths added February 2026
history_notes: ICD-10 coding from 1999 (ICD-9 for 1979-1998); single-race categories from 2018 versus bridged race 1999-2020; with the 2024 data the unreliable-rate rule changed from fewer than 20 deaths to CI width over 160% of the rate; Connecticut county rates unavailable for 2022 and later (deaths by 8 legacy counties, population by planning regions)
suppression_rules: Sub-national counts of 1-9 deaths suppressed; rates suppressed for 0-9 deaths; populations under 10 suppressed; rates flagged unreliable and hidden when the 95% CI width exceeds 160% of the rate
limitations: County detail only through the web form (no API), so automated pipelines need manual exports; small counties often suppressed unless years are pooled
doc_evidence: UCD help page: single race 2018-2024; 1-9 deaths suppressed; unreliable if CI width >160% of rate. API page: only national data can be queried via API
sample_evidence: County query needs the web form and acceptance of data-use terms (user consent required); API cannot return state or county data

name: VSRR Provisional County-Level Drug Overdose Death Counts
agency: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
description: Provisional 12-month-ending counts of drug overdose deaths by county of residence and ending month, with percent of records pending investigation, NCHS 2013 urban-rural code and completeness notes (Socrata gb4e-yj24)

history_notes: Provisional counts are revised as records arrive; deaths are reported about 6 months after death; a completeness note flags counties with low historical completeness
limitations: Counts only (no rates); provisional and incomplete, with pending investigations understating counts; overlapping 12-month windows are not independent

sample_evidence: gb4e-yj24: 226,368 rows, 3,142 counties, Jan 2020-Dec 2025; Los Angeles County 12 months ending Dec 2025 = 1,824 provisional deaths

agency: CDC National Center for Injury Prevention and Control
description: Death counts and rates per 100,000 by place of residence for drug overdose (unintentional or undetermined intent), suicide, homicide and firearm deaths, annual and trailing twelve months, from provisional and final NVSS data; rate_m flags Bayesian-modeled rates (with credible intervals) where 1-9 deaths (county Socrata psx4-wq38; national, state and tract-group files also published)
license: Public Domain U.S. Government (data.cdc.gov metadata)

doc_evidence: About page: counts and rates per 100,000 at national, state, county and tract levels; 1-9 deaths shown as a range; Bayesian model for rates with 1-9 deaths

name: SNAP Data Tables (national, state and county/project area)
agency: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration (formerly Food and Nutrition Service)
description: Administrative SNAP participation (persons, households), benefits and issuance: national annual summary 1969 onward; state monthly files FY1989 onward; bi-annual (January and July) county or project-area participation and issuance (FNS-388A)
license: No explicit license found; U.S. federal government data
time_coverage: National 1969-2025; state monthly FY1989-FY2026 (latest June 2026, preliminary); county or project area January and July 1989-July 2025
update_cadence: State tables monthly; county file twice a year (January data reported in May, July data in December)
history_notes: Recent months are preliminary and revised; large 2025-2026 changes in some states (e.g., Arizona persons 886,806 in June 2025 vs 421,147 in June 2026 initial)
limitations: Not all states report at county or project-area level and project areas may not match counties; county files are Excel sheets with a state-county-office code; figures may include disaster assistance
doc_evidence: SNAP tables page: state monthly data through June 2026; bi-annual project area/county data FY89 through July 2025; not all states report at county level
sample_evidence: FNS-388A zip (14.8 MB, 74 files): July 2025 Autauga Co AL 7,764 persons, 3,597 households, $1,513,303 issuance; US persons June 2026 initial 36,352,716

name: Feeding America Map the Meal Gap
agency: Feeding America
description: Model-based estimates of overall and child food insecurity for every county and congressional district (plus states), share of food-insecure people above and below SNAP income thresholds, food budget shortfall and county average meal cost; state-level CPS food security model with ACS and BLS predictors applied to local areas
access_requirements: Dataset released only through an online data request form (Qualtrics); interactive map is public
license: Copyright Feeding America, all rights reserved (site footer); dataset use terms not visible without submitting the request form (unverified)
time_coverage: Annual; 2026 release (published July 28, 2026) covers 2024; model uses state CPS data 2009-2024
history_notes: 2018 estimates (released 2020) added disability and a poverty measure excluding college students; 2026 release (2024 data) changed CPS aggregation and income imputation; 2023 county estimates were corrected (had used 2022 BLS unemployment)
limitations: Model predictions from state-level relationships, not local surveys; NielsenIQ food prices for meal cost; depends on CPS food security data, and USDA announced termination of future Household Food Security Reports in Sept 2025, so continuity is uncertain; variable names not verified
doc_evidence: Methodology page and 2026 Technical Brief: county and congressional district food insecurity and county food cost for 2024; state model tables 2009-2024
sample_evidence: County data only via the Data Request Form (Qualtrics); not submitted because form entry needs user consent
